limits: The temporary address makes this one destination IP local for all ports and protocols; only TCP 7000 is serviced.

Only the fixed invented local credentials can receive an experimental local profile. One initialization frame from the hash-verified user capture may then be replayed locally; this is not fresh GameGuard authentication.
At most 222 client bytes are read: version26, login91, twelve six-byte post-login headers and up to three eleven-byte property bodies. Unsupported bodies are not read.

Login and supported property bodies are decrypted only in bounded memory and then cleared. The property owner must match local account1; seven tail bytes remain uninterpreted. Credentials, packet bodies, GUIDs and tokens are never logged or saved.

At most 12294 server bytes are written: a bounded profile/clock exchange with one captured initializer, one startup acknowledgement, one zero-balance reply and up to three 3928-byte empty property replies. Unsupported headers end observation before their bodies.
The opaque initialization blob may contain old session binding. It is extracted only in memory, never saved or included in reports. Other GameGuard destinations are not isolated by the one-IP route.
ReplyWritten means the local probe handed a response to its socket; it does not prove application-level acceptance.
Closing or killing this window abruptly may leave the volatile address until CleanupLocalHandshake.cmd or a reboot.
